strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing the practical need for uncertainty quantification over scientific estimands in modern foundation models
Comprehensive empirical evaluation spanning 30 datasets with 100 repetitions, multiple regression types, and thorough supplementary analyses
Pragmatic empirical diagnostics (path stability, frequentist coverage, posterior contraction) that acknowledge theoretical limitations of deep learning verification
Competitive or superior performance across diverse experimental settings, particularly on real data and low n/p regimes
Clear presentation with well-structured motivation and detailed appendices
Honest discussion of theoretical limitations and deviations from sufficient conditions
weaknesses: Theoretical foundation is incomplete: cannot verify existence of F∞ for TabPFN; empirically demonstrates violations of both martingale and a.c.i.d. conditions; finite-sample convergence does not imply convergence to well-defined limiting distribution

Computational cost (70-200s per sample) is 3-10× higher than baselines but not adequately justified; claims of 'minimal manual intervention' are overstated given comparable automaticity of competitors
Limited theoretical contribution: observes that martingale property may be unnecessary but provides no formal characterization of necessary/sufficient conditions or convergence analysis
Significant practical limitations underexplored: TabPFN's 10,000-token context length, acknowledged difficulty with feature sampling in moderate dimensions, ad-hoc loss function engineering choices

Empirical advantages are incremental: TabMGP is competitive but not uniformly superior to baselines (especially Copula) in controlled synthetic settings; real data evaluation uses empirical distribution as ground truth, which doesn't validate performance on true data-generating distribution
Posterior shape differences (skewness/multimodality vs. Gaussian) are claimed as 'more expressive' without investigating whether this reflects model misspecification or instability
Limited comparison with concurrent work (Nagler & Rügamer 2025, Fortini et al. 2026); hyperparameter choices (N, L, covariance structure) lack sensitivity analysis
Theoretical positioning conflates an empirical heuristic with a principled inference procedure; the core claim of producing 'valid' MGP posteriors is unsubstantiated

strengths: Novel application of foundation transformers to martingale posteriors with clear practical motivation for practitioners using TabPFN
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 30 diverse settings (11 synthetic, 19 real) with 100 repetitions, including sensitivity analyses and semi-synthetic experiments
Transparent and honest treatment of theoretical limitations; well-designed empirical diagnostics (path stability, coverage, posterior contraction) provide practical tools for practitioners
Well-written paper with excellent organization and extensive supporting appendices; clear algorithm presentation and thorough experimental details support reproducibility
Pragmatic contribution showing MGP framework is more robust than previously theorized, requiring no likelihood-prior specification or extensive hyperparameter tuning unlike alternatives
weaknesses: Theoretical validity relies entirely on empirical evidence that sufficient conditions are 'stricter than necessary'—the claim that a.c.i.d. violations are due to numerical precision (Figure 5) lacks rigorous justification, creating a gap in formal guarantees

Empirical coverage is inconsistent with claims: logistic regression shows systematic undercoverage (0.78-0.91 vs target 0.95 in Table 2), particularly for GMM link functions, contradicting 'near-nominal coverage' claims
Limited scope significantly reduces impact: restricted to linear/logistic regression, small datasets (n≤200), high computational cost (70-200s vs 10-20s for copula), and TabPFN's ~10K context limit

Insufficient investigation of failure modes: paper acknowledges undercoverage with small n/p in classification but provides no principled analysis of root causes or clear guidance on when to avoid the method

Key methodological choices lack thorough justification: default N=n+500 appears arbitrary, diagonal covariance approximation due to only 100 samples is significant, and setup (e.g., fixed copula bandwidth) may disadvantage baselines

strengths: Addresses a practical need: foundation models increasingly used but lack principled uncertainty quantification
Comprehensive empirical evaluation across 30 experimental setups with diverse data types
Honest treatment of limitations: acknowledges undercoverage, computational cost, and failure modes
Well-designed experiments with multiple baselines and detailed diagnostics including path stability and posterior concentration
Clear presentation of motivation and methodology with extensive supplementary material
weaknesses: Critical theory-practice gap: central claim that MGPs work without martingale/a.c.i.d. conditions lacks rigorous justification; Appendix C shows a.c.i.d. condition is violated (Figure 5), yet dismissal as 'numerical precision' is speculative
Limited novelty: straightforward combination of existing MGP framework (Fong et al. 2023) and TabPFN (Hollmann et al. 2025) with no new theory or methods developed

Narrow experimental scope: linear and logistic regression only; single foundation model (TabPFN); small-to-moderate sample sizes only; unclear if approach generalizes to other models/loss functions/architectures

Empirical results show real limitations: undercoverage on concrete (0.91), fish (0.90), logistic (0.84); divergent trajectories in Figure 8 suggest instability with low-diversity datasets; no clear diagnostic for when method will fail

Methodological concerns: Bayesian bootstrap for features is a workaround introducing arbitrary choices; loss function specification may be as burdensome as prior specification; lack of comparison to modern uncertainty quantification methods
Computational efficiency: 70-200s per sample vs. 10-20s for copula represents 3-20× slowdown; N selection requires manual tuning despite claims of minimal intervention
No proof that F∞ converges for TabPFN; convergence diagnostics (path stability) are heuristic without theoretical grounding; relies entirely on empirical success as justification for lack of theory

strengths: Novel integration of TabPFN with martingale posterior framework addressing a real practical need for uncertainty quantification with foundation models
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 30 datasets with multiple baselines, sensitivity analyses, and semi-synthetic experiments—exemplary empirical work
Honest treatment of theoretical limitations: acknowledges violation of formal sufficient conditions and proposes reasonable empirical diagnostics instead of overselling
Clear articulation of why TabPFN specifically is well-suited (permutation invariance, Bayesian alignment, in-context learning) vs. generic transformers
Excellent reproducibility with detailed appendices covering experimental settings, hyperparameters, implementation details, and marginal/joint credible set results
Well-written paper that combines existing methods in a novel way and opens new research directions for foundation models in Bayesian inference
weaknesses: Theoretical foundation undermined: Figure 5 shows TabPFN violates a.c.i.d. condition with diverging L1-distance as N grows; dismissal as 'numerical noise' is hand-wavy; no formal characterization of when the method should work
Path stability diagnostics are post-hoc: no principled way to set rollout length N a priori; practitioners must manually inspect convergence plots; edge cases diverge at N=1000 (Figure 8)
Significant computational overhead (70-200s per sample vs. 10-20s for Copula) inadequately justified given marginal empirical improvements; no analysis of cost-benefit tradeoff

Incomplete baseline comparisons: Copula bandwidth handicapped (fixed at 0.8 due to tuning issues); classical Bayes prior sensitivity unexplored; missing comparisons to TabPFN ensembles, conformal prediction, and quantile methods
Narrow experimental scope: all functionals are linear/logistic regression; real datasets small (mostly n≤200); TabPFN's 10k-token context limit restrictive; generalization to other losses unclear

Marginal empirical gains: TabMGP competitive but not clearly superior (Tables 1-2); Copula often achieves 0.99-1.00 coverage; no significance testing; some setups favor alternatives; wins 152/293 times on marginal intervals
Limited methodological novelty: forward sampling from TabPFN is straightforward; no algorithmic contributions beyond combining existing components

Coverage evaluation for real data uses empirical distribution conflating model misspecification with finite-sample uncertainty; no ablations on Bayesian bootstrap for X, temperature parameter sensitivity, or ensemble averaging impact
